claims.statement: MessagesDatabase v7 (PR-01) adds exactly five additive tables in MIGRATION_6_7: remote_conversation_map, gateway_event_outbox, remote_commands, remote_command_executions, sync_cursors; the migration is purely additive (12 statements: 5 CREATE TABLE + 7 indexes) and GatewaySyncSchemaTest pins it against the KSP-generated 7.json.

The exactly-once/dedupe contract is enforced by three UNIQUE indexes — index_gateway_event_outbox_eventUuid, index_remote_commands_idempotencyKey, index_remote_conversation_map_threadId — and v7 creates exactly three unique indexes; GatewaySyncSchemaTest pins them by name.

Gateway payload columns are crypto-friendly from day one (ciphertext BLOB + encoding + schemaVersion + cryptoVersion); cryptoVersion=0 means UTF-8 JSON plaintext (PR-01/02) and Phase 7 (ADR-002) swaps in an opaque AEAD envelope with zero schema change, so business code must never assume the payload is readable text.

GatewaySyncRepository is a deliberately dumb boundary over the five tables with NO crypto and NO networking; upload/poll workers call its suspend functions, and its transactional claim is the process-death guarantee.

claimBatch is a transactional claim: inside db.withTransaction it selects claimable rows (state IN PENDING/SENDING and nextAttemptAt <= now, ordered by id) and calls markSending, whose SQL flips only still-PENDING rows to SENDING — making the state flip atomic with selection and a safe single-flight transition.
recoverSending() implements process-death recovery by flipping all leftover SENDING outbox rows back to PENDING (resetSendingToPending), closing the crash window between claim and ACK.

The outbox state machine is PENDING→SENDING→ACKED with SENDING→PENDING on transport failure (attemptCount+1 and backoff) and on recoverSending, and SENDING→DEAD_LETTER on permanent reject or undecodable payload; onAcked/onRetry carry WHERE state='SENDING' guards while dead-letter is unconditional.
Unique eventUuid dedupe: gateway_event_outbox uses INSERT OR IGNORE on a unique eventUuid index so re-committing an event is a no-op, never a duplicate.

Partial ACK (LOCK 13): markAcked moves only the reported eventUuid to ACKED (WHERE eventUuid=... AND state='SENDING'), so other events in a partially-accepted batch stay and retry on their own backoff.
DEAD_LETTER is a visible, queryable terminal state that is never a silent drop; dead-lettered rows are retained as the health-alert surface.

The LOCK-13 batch policy caps a batch at MAX_BATCH_EVENTS=100 events and MAX_BATCH_BYTES=512 KiB of payload bytes, but skips the byte check for the first row so a lone oversized event (>512 KiB) still ships alone and the queue never wedges.
Full-jitter exponential backoff returns a uniform random value in [0, min(cap, base·2^attempt)) with BACKOFF_BASE_MS=2000 and BACKOFF_CAP_MS=5 min, attempt clamped to 0..20.

Command inbox exactly-once is two-part: a unique idempotencyKey (INSERT OR IGNORE redelivery is a no-op returning the existing row's commandId) plus one remote_command_executions row per attempt as the audit trail that makes exactly-once provable.
Command state transitions are guarded: markAcceptedIfReceived is the atomic single-owner RECEIVED→ACCEPTED claim, and markState enforces a legal-from set via WHERE state IN (:fromStates).
The 24 h expiry floor (TechSpec §93) is set on enqueue (expiresAt = now + 24h) and enforced by expireStale, which flips unclaimed RECEIVED commands past expiresAt to the visible EXPIRED state.

remote_conversation_map is the ONLY home of the provider threadId ↔ opaque conversation UUID mapping (TechSpec §12); GatewaySyncRepository offers idempotent mapOrGet and ensureConversationIdForThread (which reads the row back after insert so a lost race returns the winner's UUID); GMweb ever sees only the UUID, never a phone-number-derived id.

GatewayEventFactory identity rules (TechSpec §13): payload.messageId is a stable name-UUID derived from the durable provider row identity source:providerId:createdAtMs (never from body/timestamp alone), and eventUuid is deterministic per event from kind + row identity + date so the outbox unique index turns rebuilt events into free dedupe.

GatewayEventFactory is envelope-only: outboxRow stores {ciphertextB64,encoding,schemaVersion,cryptoVersion} bytes with encoding=envelope.v1 and cryptoVersion=0, keeping PII inside the payload bytes never as envelope columns; decodePayloadEnvelope rejects any cryptoVersion != 0 (the explicit Phase 7 extension point).

EventUploader is the sole durable cloud transmitter and owns no RAM-only state: on start() its first act is recoverSending(), then each loop gates on prefs.isEnabled and a non-blank gmwebUrl (zero HTTP while gated), claims a batch, POSTs to /api/v1/agent/events/batch, and applies per-eventUuid partial ACK (acked→ACKED, missing→onRetry backoff), transport failure→requeue, permanent 4xx (400-499 excl 429)→dead-letter the whole batch, undecodable payload→dead-letter that one row only.

BackendClient is the shared HTTPS client: it reads backendUrl (build-time default https://gaitway.autonomousone.in, overridable via the GATEWAY_BACKEND_URL Gradle property) and gatewayToken, sends Authorization: Bearer <token>, rejects non-https:// URLs so the token never rides plaintext HTTP, uses 15s/30s timeouts, and returns a sealed Result so no exceptions leak to callers.

GatewayOutgoingPipeline.enqueueSendSms (PR-03) durably enqueues a SEND_SMS remote_commands row: it resolves the conversation UUID via ensureConversationIdForThread, mints commandId+messageUuid, builds a cryptoVersion=0 JSON payload with the 24h expiresAt floor, and ingests via ingestCommand; redelivery with the same idempotencyKey returns the existing command id (exactly-once).

The durable SEND_SMS pipeline is NOT the live production default: SmsSender.sendWithOutcome only takes the durable path when the ENQUEUE_ALL_SENDS rollout flag is true, and the flag defaults to false, so production sends still take the direct SmsManager path; when the flag is on, the command is claimed via markCommandAcceptedIfReceived and transitioned to COMPLETED/FAILED.

The outbound event path is live end to end: TelephonySyncCoordinator commits the matching cloud event inside the SAME Room transaction as the message it describes (upsert only when the row is new, plus delete/status-change/thread-read), and EventUploader is instantiated in GatewayService.onCreate and driven by ConnectionSupervisor (startEventUploader/stopEventUploader).

The fire-and-forget cloud leg is gone: WebhookEngine's KDoc carries PR-02 language but only the user-configured local webhook remains — best-effort, consent-gated via GatewayAccessPolicy.canTransmit, HTTPS-only, optional HMAC X-Signature; the durable outbox, not the webhook, is now the event path.

Gaps vs ADR targets, verified from source: the SmsSender.sendOrEnqueue shim referenced in the pipeline KDoc does not exist (the funnel is sendWithOutcome); there is no drain executor (commands execute inline, nothing polls remote_commands for RECEIVED rows); no production caller inserts remote_command_executions rows; and expireStale and the sync_cursors accessors have no production callers yet.

The design is anchored to the ADRs: ADR-001 (Android is the trust root; signed trust registry), ADR-002 (point-to-point command encryption, conversation key epochs, cryptoVersion swap), and ADR-003 (correctness = durable command + eventual pickup + no duplicate execution, with the <3s pickup SLO defined only when the agent is AGENT_AVAILABLE); the unifying principle is that correctness lives in the queue, not on the wire.

Focused JVM tests pin the layer: GatewaySyncSchemaTest (additive 6→7 migration and the three unique indexes), GatewaySyncPolicyTest (LOCK-13 batch/byte/backoff bounds), and GatewayEventFactoryTest (deterministic §13 identity, envelope round-trip, cryptoVersion=1 rejection).
